To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) the copy number of rDNA genes is reduced in human adipose with age; and (2) 5S and the 28S genes are preferentially lost in human adipose during ageing.
the loss of 5.5 and 28S genes is a preferential event during ageing and that the loss of the 18s gene copy number is preferential in obese individuals.
the copy number of two of the three rRNA genes in human adipocytes decreases with age.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of ageing and obesity in post-mitosis human tissue, and it may be useful in future studies of ageing and obesity.
the effects of aging and obesity on the human rDNA locus and the possible implications of rDNA gene loss.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the loss of rDNA genes in post-mitotically differentiated human adipocytes is a process that is accelerated by aging and body mass index and that it is preferential for the 5S and the 28S genes.
ageing and/or adiposity may induce a selective loss of the rDNA gene 5.8 S and 28S in human adipose tissues.
ageing and fat accumulation are associated with the preferential loss of rDNA genes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the loss of 5.5S and 18.5S rDNA genes may contribute to ageing and/or obesity.
the loss of 5.5S and 2.8S genes is associated with ageing and the loss of 18S gene is associated with fat accumulation.
the loss of 5.5S and 18 genes in human adipocytes is associated with ageing and/or fat deposition.

rDNA loss is an important process in human ageing.
